question: Google Maps renames Lake Ontario to "Lake America" in 2026?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Google Maps displays "Lake America," "Lake of America" or similar as the label for the body of water currently known as the "Lake Ontario" for the majority of users within the United States by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Changes which appear only in experimental features, beta versions, or subnational regional variants, will not qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

If both "Lake America" and "Lake Ontario" are used to label the body of water, this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be Google Maps (maps.google.com) however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

# Research report 1 of 2

# Lake Ontario renamed "Lake America" on Google Maps: research brief (as of 2026-08-29)

Note: many search results were dated after 2026-08-29. I left them out as instructed. Most direct page fetches failed because the proxy refused the connection, so the facts below come from search-result summaries of articles dated on or before the cutoff.

## 1. Resolution source
- Resolution is decided by Google Maps (maps.google.com) as seen by most US users, or by a consensus of credible reporting. I could not load or check Google Maps directly, so I have no pre-cutoff screenshot or reading of the label.
- 2025-02-10 (precedent): Google said it has a "longstanding practice of applying name changes when they have been updated in official government sources," meaning the federal Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) for the US. With the Gulf of America it used a split label: US users saw the US name, Mexico saw "Gulf of Mexico," and everyone else saw both. [KATV](https://www.katv.com/news/nation-world/google-updates-its-maps-to-reflect-new-gulf-of-america-name-denali-executive-order-trump-super-bowl-mexico), [Boston.com](https://www.boston.com/news/national-news/2025/02/11/google-maps-now-shows-gulf-of-america-for-u-s-users/)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-08-27: Trump signed Executive Order 14422, which renames Lake Ontario "Lake America" for federal use. Trump called it "official, effective immediately." [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-administration/trump-orders-lake-ontario-renamed-lake-america-canada-trade-war-rcna594750), [GV Wire](https://gvwire.com/2026/08/27/trump-signs-order-to-rename-lake-ontario-as-lake-america/), [Star-Advertiser](https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/08/27/photo-gallery/trump-signs-executive-order-to-rename-lake-ontario-to-lake-america/)
- What the order says: the Interior Secretary must work with the Board on Geographic Names to rename the lake and update GNIS. The order binds only the federal government, not Canada or private companies. [Federal Register public inspection](https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-18020.pdf), [GovInfo](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202600563/html/DCPD-202600563.htm)
- The trigger Google has used before (a GNIS update) is now formally required by the order. I could not confirm from a pre-cutoff source exactly when GNIS was updated or what Google had said by 2026-08-29.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-29: Ontario Premier Doug Ford answered with a 24x12 ft billboard near Grimsby reading "Lake Ontario. Now and Always." [Local10/AP](https://www.local10.com/news/world/2026/08/29/ontario-premier-answers-trumps-lake-america-with-giant-lake-ontario-sign/), [ABC/AP](https://abcnews.com/International/wireStory/ontario-premier-answers-trumps-lake-america-giant-lake-136060710)
- ~2026-08-27/28: Canadian officials, including PM Mark Carney, rejected the rename. Carney said it is Lake Ontario "then, now and always." [CBC](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/trump-lake-ontario-america-9.7322947)
- 2026-08-27: Trump signed the order in the Oval Office and tied it to the trade war, saying Canada has been "ripping us off." [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/Politics/trump-signs-executive-order-renaming-lake-ontario-lake/story?id=136009323)
- Earlier (exact date not confirmed): during a feud with Ford, Trump first floated the rename as under "serious consideration." [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/Politics/trump-floats-renaming-lake-ontario-lake-america-denies/story?id=135932301)

## 4. Base rates
- This is the closest precedent:
  - 2025-01-20: an executive order renamed the Gulf of Mexico.
  - 2025-02-09: GNIS was updated.
  - 2025-02-10: Google Maps showed "Gulf of America" to US users, about 3 weeks after the order and 1 day after GNIS changed. [KATV](https://www.katv.com/news/nation-world/google-updates-its-maps-to-reflect-new-gulf-of-america-name-denali-executive-order-trump-super-bowl-mexico)
- Counterpoint from the same period: as of 2025-02-10, Google had not yet changed Denali to Mt. McKinley, so it did not apply every federal renaming immediately. [Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/02/11/nation/gulf-of-america-google-maps-gulf-of-mexico)
- Unlike the Gulf, Lake Ontario is a shared border lake managed jointly with Canada. Under the Gulf precedent, Google would probably use a split label. The resolution criteria allow a split label and dual labels, but changes that appear only in "subnational regional variants" do not count.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket has an event, "Google Maps renames Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' by...? 2026." I could not get a price snapshot from before the cutoff. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/google-maps-renames-lake-ontario-to-lake-america-in-2026)
- Kalshi has "When will Google Maps display 'Lake America'?" A cached snapshot of unknown date, possibly from before the order, showed about 27% before Sep 15, 51% before Oct 1 and 67% before Jan 1, 2027. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxgooglelake/google-maps-displays-lake-america/kxgooglelake-27)
- A secondary source mentioned a Manifold market at about 83%. I could not confirm its date. [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/?p=18166)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (Dec 31, 2026)
- GNIS entry update by USGS and the Board on Geographic Names, as the order directs. In the Gulf case, this was what set off Google's change.
- Any statement or blog post from Google about how it will label the lake (US-only, split or dual).
- Canadian diplomatic or legal pushback, and how the US-Canada trade war develops.
- The US midterm elections in November 2026, which are unlikely to affect the federal naming directly.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I'm writing up the findings now. I have enough material dated on or before 2026-08-29. I left out all reporting published after that date.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-08-29: The deciding source is Google Maps (maps.google.com). I couldn't load it directly because the proxy refused the connection, so I can't confirm the label it currently shows.
- 2026-08-29 (Saturday): Google published a post titled "How the GNIS Lake Ontario/Lake America name change in the U.S. will appear in Maps." It says the U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS, the federal naming database) has formally changed "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" in the United States, and that Google follows GNIS names. According to the post, U.S. users will see "Lake America," Canadian users will see "Lake Ontario," and users elsewhere will see both names. The search summary says the rollout started that Saturday. I couldn't open the post itself (proxy refused), so these details come from search summaries. [Google blog](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/maps/gnis-lake-ontario-lake-america-name-change/)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-08-29: Google has publicly committed to showing "Lake America" to U.S. users and says the rollout is starting. Showing both names also counts as Yes under the criteria. Nothing I found dated on or before 2026-08-29 says the rollout was finished or reached most U.S. users. That gap is the main thing left to check. [Google blog](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/maps/gnis-lake-ontario-lake-america-name-change/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-29: Ontario Premier Doug Ford answered with a billboard on the Canadian shore reading "Lake Ontario. Now and forever." [Wikipedia: naming dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Ontario_naming_dispute)
- 2026-08-29: Google's blog post on following the GNIS change (see section 1). [Google blog](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/maps/gnis-lake-ontario-lake-america-name-change/)
- Late Aug 2026 (exact date unclear): Canadian officials, including Prime Minister Mark Carney, rejected the name and called it "real foolishness." Several U.S. state officials also reportedly rejected it. [CBC](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/trump-lake-ontario-america-9.7322947), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Ontario_naming_dispute)
- 2026-08-27: Trump signed Executive Order 14422, directing federal agencies to use "Lake America" for Lake Ontario. This came during the trade war with Canada. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Ontario_naming_dispute)
- 2026-08-25: Trump first floated the name. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Ontario_naming_dispute)
- Background: a Congressional Research Service (CRS) report says federal naming decisions don't legally bind private companies. Google relies on its own GNIS-following policy instead. (Fortune, via search summary)

## 4. Base rates
- 2025-01/02, Gulf of Mexico: Trump ordered the rename to "Gulf of America" in January 2025. Google said it would follow GNIS, and it switched the U.S. label within roughly a day of the GNIS update in early February 2025. U.S. users saw the new name, Mexican users the old one, and others both. Google did the same for Mount McKinley/Denali. That is the same policy and three-way regional split now announced for the lake.
- In every recent case I know of where GNIS formally changed a name on executive order, Google adopted it for U.S. users within days. I found no case where Google announced a GNIS-driven label change and then didn't carry it out.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-08-29: Tech Insider cites a Manifold (play-money) market on the Google question at about 83% Yes. It also says a related Polymarket market exists, but I couldn't find its price. [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/?p=18166)
- Late Aug 2026: Action Network says Polymarket traders are betting on when Apple Maps will rename the lake, with near-term dates priced at about 56-66%. [Action Network](https://www.actionnetwork.com/politics/when-will-apple-maps-rename-lake-ontario-to-lake-america)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (2026-12-31)
- Whether Google finishes the rollout to most U.S. users across web and app. Partial or staggered rollouts are the main near-term uncertainty.
- Possible reversals: GNIS or the executive order being changed, court challenges, or a shift in Canada-U.S. trade talks. I found no reporting of any of these as of 2026-08-29.
- Pressure on Google from Canada or U.S. states. Google says it follows GNIS, so outside pressure would probably need a GNIS change to alter the label.

Sources:
- [Google blog](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/maps/gnis-lake-ontario-lake-america-name-change/)
- [CBC](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/trump-lake-ontario-america-9.7322947)
- [Wikipedia: Lake Ontario naming dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Ontario_naming_dispute)
- [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/?p=18166)
- [Action Network](https://www.actionnetwork.com/politics/when-will-apple-maps-rename-lake-ontario-to-lake-america)

summaries.
- February 10, 2025: Google stated its longstanding practice of following GNIS, and applied it to the Gulf one day after the GNIS update.
- Markets: Manifold was at about 83%, and an undated Kalshi snapshot (possibly from before the order) showed about 67% before January 1, 2027.

For No:
- The other research report did not find the Google blog post or confirm a GNIS update.
- A GNIS update two days after the order would be much faster than the Gulf case, which took about three weeks.
- The lake is shared with Canada, and Canadian and some US state officials have rejected the name.
- No pre-cutoff source confirms the rollout reached most US users.

**(e) Scenarios**
- No: the blog post summary is wrong or premature, GNIS is delayed or blocked by a court challenge or a trade deal that withdraws the rename, and Google keeps "Lake Ontario" through year-end.
- Yes: GNIS is updated, Google applies its standard policy, and US users see "Lake America" within days, as with the Gulf.

**(f) From base rate to final**
I start at about 87% from the precedents. I move up for the reported Google announcement and rollout start, and because four months is ample time for a process that took three weeks last time. I hold back slightly because the blog post is unverified and uncorroborated by the other report, and because a legal or diplomatic reversal is possible. The near-term listed resolution date is also consistent with an early Yes. That puts me at about 95%.

Probability: 95%
